analyzed_vuln.description: The root cause is missing bounds/validity checks on AVTAB type IDs before indexing policydb type-attribute arrays. `check_assertion_avtab_match()` directly uses `k->source_type - 1` and `k->target_type - 1` to index `p->attr_type_map[...]` (lines 462, 473, 483) and passes those ebitmap pointers to `ebitmap_match_any()`. With malformed policy input, a type value can be 0 or otherwise invalid, making the index negative/underflowed or out of range, so `ebitmap_match_any()` dereferences an out-of-bounds ebitmap node pointer and triggers a heap-buffer-overflow read. Crash occurs in `ebitmap_match_any`, but unsafe state propagation originates in `check_assertion_avtab_match`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered during neverallow assertion checking (`cil_check_neverallow` -> `check_assertion` -> `avtab_map` -> `check_assertion_avtab_match`) when fuzzed CIL input creates AVTAB entries with invalid source/target type IDs relative to `p->p_types.nprim`/`attr_type_map` size. Because `check_assertion_avtab_match` does not validate that `k->source_type` and `k->target_type` are within [1, nprim], it can index before/after `attr_type_map` and pass corrupted ebitmap objects to `ebitmap_match_any`, causing OOB read.
